q: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
That's the student ___ essay won the prize.
The town ___ I was born is very small.
e: Place + clause with its own subject: where.

q: My father, ___ is 70, still works.
e: Non-defining clause about a person: who (never 'that' after a comma).

q: I didn't understand ___ he said.
The book ___ I bought yesterday is excellent.
He failed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
e: ', which' refers to the whole previous idea.

q: The people ___ live in this area are very friendly. (one word)
e: Defining clause about people: who or that.

q: 2020 was the year ___ everything changed. (one word)
The company, ___ employs 500 people, is expanding. (one word)
e: Non-defining clause about a thing: which.

q: She has two brothers, both of ___ are engineers. (one word)
e: After 'both of / all of / none of' use whom (people) or which (things).

q: This is the reason ___ I left. (one word)
The man ___ car was stolen called the police. (one word)
The film who we saw last night was boring.
fix: The film which we saw last night was boring.

q: This is the book that I told you about it.
fix: This is the book that I told you about.
e: 'That' already stands for the book: do not repeat it.

q: The teacher which helped me most was Mr Lopez.
fix: The teacher who helped me most was Mr Lopez.

q: I like people what are honest.
fix: I like people who are honest.

q: I met a woman. Her son is a pilot.
hint: Join with 'whose'. Begin: I met a woman ...
a: I met a woman whose son is a pilot.

q: The hotel was very clean. We stayed there.
a: The hotel where we stayed was very clean.

q: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia. It has eight million inhabitants.
hint: Join with a non-defining clause. Begin: Bogotá, which ...
a: Bogotá, which is the capital of Colombia, has eight million inhabitants.
Bogotá, which has eight million inhabitants, is the capital of Colombia.
e: Extra information goes between commas with 'which'.
